title: Linux headless key custody: TPM2-sealed vault key through tpm2-tools, gated on its T26 run (DEC-262)
description: Operator ruling 2026-09-28, relayed by opum-agent (OPAG-675) and binding once opum-doc records it: Ward's committed platforms are macOS, Linux and Windows, matching lore and quest. The first developer preview stays macOS-only. Linux needs a verified, persistent, protected native backend (Secret Service, or another backend that meets spec §6.4). Never a plaintext file or a session-only store. A headless machine without a usable backend fails closed with actionable guidance. Linux is not advertised until its own T26 qualification run passes (spec line 38). Do not build this before WCLI-5 and WCLI-6.

acceptanceCriteria.text: On a headless Linux host whose TPM2 is reachable at /dev/tpmrm0 (never /dev/tpm0), a Linux KeyProvider seals the 32-byte vault key itself to the TPM through tpm2-tools. It keeps the sealed public and private blobs and contexts user-private (0600, in Ward's 0700 directory), with no PCR binding. The key unseals after the process and the host restart with nobody present, and cannot be unsealed off-host. The vault format is unchanged (DEC-255 a6). The backend and TPM path are named and measured the way WCLI-5 measured the macOS Keychain.

The vault key reaches tpm2-tools only on a pipe: tpm2_create reads it on stdin and tpm2_unseal writes it on stdout, which Ward reads directly. It never appears in argv, a temp file or the environment. The unseal runs in a salted HMAC session, so the unsealed key never crosses the TPM interface in clear. Tests prove these three properties, and a mocked test does not stand in for the T26 run. If the installed tpm2-tools cannot run the unseal in a salted HMAC session, the slice stops and returns to opum-doc; the libtss2 (bun:ffi) fallback is used only on opum-doc's ruling.

Ward detects the capability by presence, not version. A host without tpm2-tools, without /dev/tpmrm0, or without access to it refuses by name and fails closed in bounded time, naming what to install or which group to join. It never falls back to a plaintext file, a session-only store (including the kernel keyutils keyring) or systemd-creds host-key-only mode. The status and doctor reports say which of three states a host is in: TPM2 absent (unsupported), TPM2 present but not accessible to this user (a named host configuration step), or the blob not user-private. The WCLI-21 ADR states that supported hosts need the tpm2-tools package, and states the threat model: it protects against copying the blob off the host and against other non-root users, not against root or an attacker who boots the same machine.

T26 on a headless Linux host (jetson): a real TPM2 seal-and-unseal integration run and a packaged-binary smoke test pass, including a reboot, and the daemon's effective groups are recorded in the run. Linux is advertised only after that run, and the run is cited where it is advertised. spark stays unsupported by presence until it exposes a TPM2. Desktop-Linux Secret Service is a separate, unadvertised task until it has its own measured T26.

implementationNotes: From WCLI-5: the Keychain adapter fails closed with vault_key_store_unsupported on any platform other than darwin, before constructing an entry. Reason: on Linux, @napi-rs/keyring silently falls back to the kernel keyutils keyring, which does not survive a reboot (per the binding's README). When this task lands, pin the entry explicitly to Secret Service (EntryOptions linux.store) and lift the darwin-only check for that backend alone.

The platform ruling is recorded in opum-doc as ODOC-316 (docs/adr/wards-committed-platform-target-macos-linux-and-windows.md, opum-doc main 900319d), and this repository's docs/adr/0004-committed-platform-target.md states it (WCLI-23).

WCLI-20 review, 2026-09-28: the non-darwin setup lock fallback (O_EXCL file + dead-pid reaping, src/adapters/setup-session.ts) carries a measured check-then-delete race — 12 overlapping holder pairs in 20 rounds, measured by the independent reviewer with process.platform faked. Unreachable today because the key provider refuses non-darwin. Before any platform is qualified, replace the fallback with kernel-arbitrated locking (fcntl F_SETLK, as flock(2) via bun:ffi already does on macOS) or identity-checked compare-and-delete.
Grooming 2026-10-28 (opum-doc approved via team-lead): re-ranked to low, kept.

REWORDED 2026-11-08 under DEC-262 (a9), with (a2) and DEC-255 (a6): the headless backend is a TPM2-sealed vault key through tpm2-tools, replacing the earlier Secret Service KeyProvider framing. Rulings: (a1) build it now, T26 on jetson, spark unsupported by presence; (a2) /dev/tpmrm0 only, access by host configuration, direct to the TPM, blob user-private, doctor reports three states; (a9) Q1 tpm2-tools with the key only on pipes, a salted HMAC session for the unseal, capability detected by presence, libtss2 via bun:ffi only on opum-doc ruling; Q2 no PCR binding; Q3 the vault key itself is sealed, so the vault format is unchanged (DEC-255 a6). WCLI-152 (Linux setup lock) is a prerequisite. Desktop-Linux Secret Service is a separate task. The earlier AC text and the WCLI-5 and WCLI-20 notes above it are history.

SLICE 2 DESIGN NOTE 2026-11-08, from the #294 review (finding 7): the setup lock lives on an open file description. A child spawned while it is held (for example tpm2-tools run by a TPM provider) shares that description if the fd lacks close-on-exec, and keeps the lock held after the parent exits. That costs liveness, not safety: it never lets two processes hold the lock. Slice 2 must confirm that Bun openSync sets O_CLOEXEC, or that its spawns do not pass inherited fds, and test it. Also carried into slice 2 (opum-doc, DEC-262 a9): a fresh salted session for every unseal with tpm2_sessionconfig decrypt/encrypt reported as a pass/fail check, and Ward sets and verifies 0600 itself on every blob and context file it writes.
